;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]], [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**A [[Syrian Air Force]] [[Aero L-39 Albatros|L-39]] jet aircraft is shot down by a [[Turkish Air Force]] [[General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon|F-16]] near the [[Syria–Turkey border]]. [http://www.syriahr.com/?p=366778 (SOHR)], [https://www.rt.com/news/482181-idlib-syria-turkey-plane (RT)]
**Turkey says it will deploy its domestically-produced [[surface-to-air missile]] [[HISAR (surface to air missile system)|HISAR]] to Syria's [[Idlib Governorate]] next week. [https://www.star.com.tr/savunma/ssb-baskani-mujdeyi-verdi-hisar-hava-savunma-sistemi-1-haftaya-sahada-olacak-haber-1519566/ (Star)]
**[[Syrian government]] sources say a Turkish drone was shot down by the [[Syrian Air Defense Force]] near Idlib; subsequent footage shared by the source shows drone to be a [[Bayraktar Tactical UAS|Bayraktar TB1]]. [https://en.muraselon.com/2020/03/syrian-army-retakes-the-large-city-of-saraqib-in-south-idlib/ (Muraselon)]
**Four [[Turkish soldier]]s are killed and seven are wounded in Tranbeh, west of Saraqeb by [[Syrian Army]] shelling; some are transferred to Turkish hospitals in [[Reyhanlı]] by helicopter. [http://www.syriahr.com/en/?p=156324 (SOHR)] [http://www.syriahr.com/?p=366961 (SOHR)]
**Twenty-six Syrian Army troops are killed by Turkish ground and drone strikes, raising the number of pro-Syrian government forces killed by Turkey in the past five days to 139. [http://www.syriahr.com/?p=366819 (SOHR)] [http://www.syriahr.com/?p=366818 (SOHR)]
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**The [[Government of National Accord|GNA government]] says all flights from [[Mitiga International Airport]], the only functioning airport in the capital [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], will be shifted to [[Misrata Airport]] after [[Libyan National Army]] forces struck the airport with rockets. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-libya-security/libya-shifts-flights-from-tripoli-to-misrata-amid-heavier-bombing-idUKKBN20Q343 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*Australian [[news agency]] [[Australian Associated Press]] (AAP) announces it will be closing down at the end of June, after 85 years of operation. [https://apnews.com/c9d2809aaa0e8fa47c629723444d7b51 (AP)]
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**In an emergency move, its first since 2008, the U.S. [[Federal Reserve]] cuts the [[federal funds rate]] by 0.5%, to a range between 1 and 1.25%. [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/fed-cuts-rates-by-50-basis-points-amid-coronavirus-concerns-150008506.html (Yahoo Finance)]
**U.S. stocks extend their drop in response to the cuts. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/global-stocks-gain-on-stimulus-hopes-11583206230 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020|United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020]]
**Three [[tornado]]es, two at least [[Enhanced Fujita scale#Parameters|EF 3]] in strength, rip through downtown [[Nashville]] and surrounding towns, killing 25 people. [https://www.wkrn.com/news/nashville-tornado/possible-tornado-crosses-through-downtown-nashville-widespread-damage-reported/ (WKRN)] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/weather/2020/03/03/nashville-tennessee-tornado-kills-downs-power-lines-and-buildings/4936988002/ (''USA Today'')]
**The state of [[Tennessee]] declares a [[state of emergency]] over the outbreak. [https://www.wbir.com/article/news/local/tn-emergency-management-agency-announces-state-of-emergency/51-009e70a6-d68d-408f-91fa-3aa6d124f4b0 (WBIR)]
**[[John C. Tune Airport]] sustained major damage from the outbreak. [https://www.foxnews.com/us/nashville-tornado-damage-plane-severe-weather-tossed-tennessee (Fox News)]
**[[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump|Trump]] announces he will visit [[Tennessee]] on Friday. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2020/03/03/nashville-tornado/ (''Washington Post'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] declares "war" on the coronavirus. [https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/live-blog/coronavirus-updates-live-countries-prepare-outbreak-spreads-n1143556 (NBC)]
***Myanmar turns a [[Silversea Cruises]] [[cruise ship]] away due to fears of coronavirus, a government spokesman says. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-myanmar-ship/myanmar-turns-away-cruise-ship-over-coronavirus-fears-idUSKBN20Q1CQ?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] announces it will cancel ceremonies marking the anniversary of the [[2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami|2011 earthquake and tsunami]] as a precaution against the spread of coronavirus. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-japan-ceremony/japan-to-cancel-ceremony-marking-deadly-quake-as-coronavirus-spreads-media-idUSKBN20Q24Q (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[Ukraine]] reports its first case. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-ukraine/ukraine-reports-first-coronavirus-case-health-official-idUSKBN20Q0ZH (Reuters)]
***[[Spain|Spanish]] authorities announce that the first death from COVID-19 in the country occurred in [[Valencia]] on February 13. [https://www.elmundo.es/ciencia-y-salud/salud/2020/03/03/5e5e0900fc6c83af188b45bd.html (''El Mundo'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-spain-death/spain-confirms-countrys-first-death-from-coronavirus-health-official-idUSKBN20Q2TG (Reuters)]
***[[Liechtenstein]] reports its first case. [https://www.vaterland.li/liechtenstein/vermischtes/erster-positiv-getesteter-corona-verdachtsfall;art171,413173 (''Vaterland'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
***[[Iran]] says it will release 54,000 prisoners in an effort to prevent the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in overcrowded jails. Only inmates who test negative for COVID-19 will be allowed to leave prison and those sentenced to longer than five years will not be freed. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-51723398 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)]]
***Two people who died in the [[Seattle]] area on February 26 are found to have died from COVID-19, bringing the total death toll in the state of [[Washington (state)|Washington]] to nine. [https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2020/03/03/811690163/9-coronavirus-deaths-now-reported-in-washington-state (NPR)]
**A [[Twitter]] human resources official advises that Twitter employees [[work-at-home|work at home]] to prevent exposure to [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2]]. He adds that telecommuting will be mandatory for employees based in the Twitter offices in [[Hong Kong]], Japan, and South Korea. [https://sputniknews.com/world/202003031078457180-twitter-advises-employees-to-work-from-home-to-avoid-exposure-to-coronavirus/ (Sputnik)]
**[[Argentina]] reports its first case. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-argentina/argentine-health-minister-confirms-countrys-first-case-of-coronavirus-idUSKBN20Q2SC (Reuters)]
**[[Chile]] confirms its first case of COVID-19 in the Maule region. [https://www.biobiochile.cl/noticias/nacional/region-del-maule/2020/03/03/confirman-primer-caso-de-coronavirus-en-chile.shtml/ (BioBio in Spanish)]

;International relations
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**[[Ministry of the Interior (Turkey)|Turkish interior minister]] says over 130,000 refugees have crossed into [[Greece]] in the past four days. [https://www.trthaber.com/haber/gundem/bakan-soylu-130469-gocmen-yunanistana-gecti-464437.html (TRT Haber)]

;Law and crime
*A court in [[Kazakhstan]] orders the early release of [[Mukhtar Dzhakishev]], the former CEO of state nuclear firm [[Kazatomprom]], who had been sentenced to 14 years in prison for corruption in 2010. Upon his release he will have served more than 11 years in prison. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-kazakhstan-dzhakishev/kazakh-court-frees-ex-ceo-of-state-nuclear-firm-idUSKBN20Q0I8 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]], [[2020 Republican Party presidential primaries]]
**Voters in 14 [[U.S. state]]s and [[American Samoa]] go to the polls in this year's [[Super Tuesday#2020|Super Tuesday]]. [https://www.vox.com/2020/3/2/21142609/super-tuesday-2020-polls-delegates-contested-convention (''Vox'')]
**Former [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Joe Biden]] is the night's big winner with victories in ten states, while [[United States Senate|Senator]] [[Bernie Sanders]] wins four and former [[Mayor of New York City|New York City Mayor]] [[Michael Bloomberg]] wins American Samoa. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/03/04/politics/super-tuesday-takeaways/index.html (CNN)]
